headline: Core demand holds, margin slips on mix and vehicle-ID drag
summary_short: Vontier's Q1 2026 revenue rose 1.3% y/y to $750.6M on 1.7% core sales growth, but fell 7.2% q/q, while adjusted operating margin slipped 70bp y/y to 21.0% and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.66 was down 22.4% q/q despite a 11.9% y/y gain.
summary_long: Revenue grew 1.3% y/y to $750.6M (core sales +1.7%) on strong Environmental & Fueling Solutions demand (+4.5%), while Mobility Technologies slipped 0.4% on lower vehicle-identification shipments and Repair Solutions was flat amid mix and a bad-debt reserve. Adjusted operating margin fell 70bp y/y to 21.0%; adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.80 from $0.77. Net income of $94.3M and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.66 both improved y/y but fell sharply q/q. Operating cash flow dropped to $46.5M from $110.4M y/y and cash fell to $233.8M as the company retired its $499.8M current debt tranche. The company reaffirmed FY2026 guidance (sales $2,990-$3,040M, adjusted EPS $3.35-$3.50) and initiated Q2 2026 guidance (sales $730-$740M, adjusted EPS $0.78-$0.81), alongside announcing the Teletrac Navman divestiture.

drivers.explanation: Core sales grew 1.7% y/y led by strong demand for convenience retail solutions including fueling and environmental systems and payment technologies; Environmental & Fueling Solutions core sales rose 6.1% on fuel dispensing equipment and aftermarket parts.

Mobility Technologies margin fell 260bp on lower vehicle-identification shipments partially offset by convenience-retail payment/POS demand; Repair Solutions margin fell 180bp on unfavorable mix and a bad-debt reserve.
Cash used to retire the $499.8M current portion of long-term debt this quarter, partly funded by a new $300M 364-day term loan facility entered the same day.
